name: Marpac Medical
about:
Marpac Medical operates from Albuquerque, New Mexico, where it has produced medical devices since its spin-off from Rotec in 1992. Rotec began in the 1980s manufacturing tracheostomy tube holders and orthopedic products for DePuy; when DePuy acquired the orthopedic division, the tracheostomy holder business became the privately held Marpac.

The company manufactures FDA Class 1 medical devices, specifically endotracheal (ET) tube holders and tracheostomy tube holders. All products are designed and produced at its Albuquerque facility without outsourcing, a structure the company says allows strict quality control and rapid response to customer needs. Marpac aims to keep all items in stock and typically ships orders within one to two days.

Its distributor network includes New Start Home Medical Equipment, Timberlake Medical, Affordable Medical Supply, and Medical Specialties Distributors.

Founded on principles of quality, affordability, innovation, and customer service, Marpac was created to develop products that improve patient care while remaining easy for medical staff and families to use.

name: Mars Plastics
old_description: Impeccable Customer Service with each customer assigned their own inside representative
about:
Mars Plastics operates from Providence, Rhode Island, with a second facility in nearby Cranston. The company has over 50 years of injection molding experience and remains a family-owned business passed through generations. Founded as a molding operation, it has grown into one of the largest injection molders on the East Coast, serving customers ranging from individual inventors to major retailers.

The company runs a 100,000-square-foot facility operating 24 hours a day, seven days a week. Its equipment lineup includes 40 injection molding machines — 36 in Providence and four in Cranston — ranging from 12 to 1,400 tons of clamping force with shot capacities up to 160 ounces. Core processes cover conventional injection molding, gas-assist molding, over-molding, insert molding, and two-color molding. In-house capabilities extend to tool design and machining, design engineering with CAD and simulation, finishing (trimming, painting, printing, plating), assembly, and work-cell manufacturing that integrates decorating and packaging. A recent addition is 3D printing for rapid prototyping and low-volume production.

Mars Plastics serves retail giants such as Target and Walmart as an authorized manufacturer, along with a broad base of corporate clients and startup inventors. The company has helped numerous small concepts scale into industry leaders and has guided established corporations in reshoring production from overseas to its Rhode Island plants. Its contract manufacturing services support third-party brands across consumer goods and other sectors.

The company emphasizes a dedicated inside representative for every customer, continuous reinvestment in new molding machines and robotic automation, and a quality system that retains first and last shots from each run alongside statistical process control. Work-cell manufacturing is cited as a key differentiator that allows Mars to compete with overseas facilities on cost and lead time.

about:
Martel Inc was founded on July 2, 1984, in Dover, Delaware, by Mark B. Carlson. The family-owned company began as a one-man operation out of a garage, aiming to provide reliable telecommunications solutions for businesses on the Delmarva Peninsula.

Today, Martel operates from a commercial facility in Dover with a fully stocked parts warehouse and offers 24/7 service. The company provides cloud-based VOIP, legacy telecommunications, video surveillance systems, access control, and structured cabling for computer and telephone networks. A full staff of technicians and sales personnel handles installation, maintenance, and support.

Martel serves businesses across Delmarva and southeastern Pennsylvania, including clients such as Delaware Grange Mutual Insurance Company, Parsell Funeral Homes & Crematorium, Surgical Associates, and the Delaware Surgery Center. Its customer base spans industries needing commercial phone systems, security cameras, legacy telecom, and network cabling.

The founder started the business to fill a gap for reputable, responsive telecom service. The company emphasizes an old-fashioned, live customer-service approach—personalized, prompt, and focused on solving problems—as its primary differentiator against larger national competitors.

Maryland Community Solar operates from Columbia, Maryland, as a locally owned, family-run enterprise led by CEO Tony Napolitano. The company was established to educate Maryland residents and businesses about community solar programs and to simplify enrollment in those programs.

The firm provides consumer education on the benefits of community solar, assesses eligibility, and guides customers through the enrollment process. A customer relations team works directly with homeowners, renters, and businesses, including those served by third-party energy suppliers, to explain how subscription to a local solar farm can reduce electric bills by 5% to 25%. The company coordinates with solar developers and utility providers to facilitate the subscription and billing process.

The organization states its mission is to make Maryland a leader in sustainability and renewable energy through honest communication, by example, and caring for customers and communities.

The Maryland Food Center Authority (MFCA) operates from Jessup, Maryland, where it oversees the Maryland Food Center, a centralized hub for wholesale food distribution.

The authority manages two primary facilities—the Maryland Wholesale Produce Market and the Maryland Market Center—leasing space to a roster of wholesale merchants selling fruits, vegetables, and seafood.

The center serves the broader food industry, including wholesale produce distributors, seafood suppliers, and a single retail seafood vendor open to the public. The MFCA’s mission is to maximize the efficiency of Maryland’s food distribution network and ensure the state’s future food supply through coordinated public-private development. Its vision aims for the most modern, safe, and efficient food distribution network in the world.

Its management team brings combined experience across all aspects of the orthopedic market, and the company emphasizes education for both its sales agents and clinical customers.

The company states that its differentiation lies in a commitment to excellence, high-quality products and service, and a leadership role in education. about:
Matchless Plastics operates from Plymouth, Minnesota, where it has provided custom plastic injection molding for nearly four decades. The company began as a small operation and grew into a manufacturing partner serving customers nationwide, though the exact founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The shop specializes in injection molding with capabilities that include soft-touch overmolding, insert molding, custom color matching, molded internal threads, complex geometrics, and texturing. In-house CNC machining and secondary operations support tight-tolerance modifications, while assembly, pad printing, painting, and screen printing provide finished, production-ready parts. The company works with engineering-grade resins such as ABS, polycarbonate, nylon, acetal, PEEK, TPE, TPU, and glass-, carbon-, or mineral-filled materials, handling projects from prototype through large-scale production runs.

Matchless serves the heavy equipment, HVAC, consumer products, and agricultural industries. Its customer base consists of manufacturers seeking end-to-end support from design-for-manufacturability feedback through tooling, molding, and final delivery.

The company states its mission is delivering reliable, high-quality injection molding backed by exceptional service, emphasizing flexibility to accommodate last-minute changes and quick turnaround times. Core values described as grit, humbly confident, positive, and hungry guide the team's approach to problem-solving and long-term partnerships.

Matrix Corporation was founded in 1999 in Menomonee Falls, Wisconsin, just outside Milwaukee. The company began as a PCB design provider and has since grown into a full-service contract electronics manufacturer serving OEMs and engineering teams across the Midwest.

Today Matrix Corp builds printed circuit boards from single-unit prototypes through low-to-mid volume production, with no order minimums. Its facility handles PCB design, quick-turn and prototype fabrication, production runs scaling from hundreds to tens of thousands, turnkey assembly with surface-mount, through-hole, and mixed-technology processes, component sourcing, 3D AOI and X-ray inspection, functional testing, conformal coating and potting, and box-build integration of wiring, enclosures, and subsystems. The company reports thousands of unique assemblies produced and hundreds of active customers.

The manufacturer serves commercial electronics, consumer devices, telecommunications, healthcare and medical devices, and industrial equipment sectors, primarily in Wisconsin, Illinois, and the broader Midwest.

Matrix Corp emphasizes domestic manufacturing to avoid offshore lead-time surprises, a single-roof model that eliminates vendor handoffs, ISO 9001:2015 quality management with IPC-A-610 Class 2 workmanship and full traceability, and a commitment to on-time delivery. The firm traces its evolution to a focus on solving real-world manufacturing challenges for regulated and time-sensitive markets.

MB Cable Company, LLC operates from New Brunswick, New Jersey, where it assembles custom marked and bundled cable solutions for electrical contractors nationwide.

The company's core offering is custom bundle assemblies configured to jobsite specifications. Its product line includes straight assemblies, cross-tape assemblies, and break-out assemblies, supplemented by value-added services such as custom marking and identification, color striping, pulling grips, and sequential footage markers. Additional pre-fabricated items include whips, stripped lengths, and a solar quick-connect system. All conductors in a given bundle are sourced from a single manufacturer, a practice the company says ensures consistency from purchase through installation.

Its solar quick-connect product and recent blog coverage of utility-scale solar economics indicate an active presence in the renewable-energy installation sector. Typical customers are electrical contractors and project managers seeking to consolidate multiple reels into a single pull, reduce scrap, and cut labor hours spent on wire identification.

The company states its mission is to increase jobsite productivity and safety while saving time and reducing cost. By eliminating the need for multiple reels and the labor associated with ringing out and marking cables, MB Cable positions its bundled solutions as a way to avoid costly scrap wire and streamline the pulling process.

about:
Pioneer Meats operates from Big Timber, Montana, where Brian and Kary Engle established the business in 2006 on a 20-acre property. Brian’s path into meat processing began in his youth, cutting meat with his family, and later processing deer and elk for friends from a converted semi-trailer between 1993 and 1997. After earning an Animal Sciences degree from Montana State University, he and Kary restarted the venture, building a USDA-inspected facility at the current location.

The company provides custom meat processing for both domestic livestock and wild game, producing a range of cured and smoked products including snack sticks, bratwurst, bacon, sausage, hot dogs, along with proprietary sauces and spice blends. A retail store on-site sells these items directly to consumers. The facility handles cutting, grinding, curing, smoking, and packaging, though specific equipment and headcount are not disclosed.

Pioneer Meats serves individual hunters, livestock owners, and retail customers across Montana and beyond. The business is active in the meat processing industry through membership in the Montana Meat Processors Association, the North West Meat Processors Association, and the American Association of Meat Processors, with Brian Engle holding board positions in the first and third organizations.

The Engles attribute their reputation to a focus on award-winning quality; since 2005 the company has earned multiple Grand Champion titles at state and regional cured-meat shows, including Best of Show for bacon in 2009. Community involvement, from supporting local food banks to agricultural scholarships, is also cited as a core value.

Merrow emphasizes its hand‑built approach, the depth of its legacy‑parts program, and the Stitch Lab service as key differentiators. The company says its stitches bring visual impact, performance, and distinction to consumer products, and that it strives to go beyond expectations in customer relationships.

about:
Metal Industries, Inc. operates from Hartford, Connecticut, where it has been machining parts since the 1940s. The business began as Metropolitan Tool and Machine Company, founded by Vincent D. Zito at the current location on Wethersfield Avenue. The company produced components for U.S. troops during World War II. Vincent A. Zito took over in the 1950s and incorporated the firm as Metal Industries, Inc. in 1965. The shop later manufactured radiator cooling components for the Mercury Space Program space suits from 1958 to 1963. Today, the third generation, led by Vincent M. Zito, runs the operation.

Materials processed include steel, aluminum, bronze, plastics, and composites.

Customers span commercial, municipal, government, industrial, and agricultural sectors, with historical work for the aerospace industry on the Mercury program. The shop serves OEMs, provides spare parts, and handles repairs for hard-to-find components, offering emergency service outside normal hours to reduce downtime.

The company emphasizes its third-generation experience, creative problem-solving, and precise workmanship as differentiators, aiming to exceed expectations on jobs of any size.

about:
Microboard Processing, Inc. was founded in 1983 by Craig Hoekenga in Seymour, Connecticut. Before entering electronics manufacturing, Hoekenga had built a national reputation as an efficiency consultant to companies such as GE, GTE, Panasonic, IBM, and Phillips. Today the company is woman-owned, led by President and CEO Nicole Russo.

The firm provides electronics manufacturing services including circuit card assembly, system integration, and test services. It emphasizes high-reliability, high-complexity manufacturing with a focus on rigorous testing and quality. Microboard operates with a strong engineering staff, a dedicated RF test design team, and leading-edge equipment and software capable of placing the industry’s smallest components to build complex, fail-critical boards.

Microboard serves the defense, medical, telecommunications, and industrial sectors. Its customer base ranges from government contractors to innovative startups, with the company stating a focus on “life saving and life changing products.”

The company’s guiding principles—Process Excellence, Partnership, and People—underpin a self-described “zero defect culture of continuous improvement” and a motto of “brilliant together.” Microboard also highlights its commitment to humanitarian work, including wells, food, and medicine for marginalized communities, as an inseparable part of its culture.

name: Micron Semiconductor Products Inc.
old_description: Welcome to Micron.com, please Log in or Register an account to continue.
about:
Micron Semiconductor Products Inc. is headquartered in Meridian, Idaho. The company traces its origins to 1978, when a four-person team launched a semiconductor design venture in the basement of a Boise, Idaho dental office. By 1980, the founders had broken ground on their first fabrication plant, and within a few years they introduced the world’s smallest 256K DRAM.

Today Micron designs and manufactures a broad portfolio of memory and storage products, including DRAM components and modules, LPDDR, GDDR, NAND flash, NOR flash, managed NAND, multichip packages, and solid-state drives for data center, client, automotive, and industrial markets. Recent milestones include high-volume production of HBM4 for NVIDIA’s Vera Rubin platform and mass production of its sixth-generation PCIe Gen6 SSD, alongside a 245TB data-center SSD now shipping.

Micron serves customers across automotive, industrial, aerospace and defense, data center and cloud, client PC, consumer electronics, mobile, network infrastructure, industrial IoT, robotics, artificial intelligence, high-performance computing, and video security sectors.

Micron states its purpose is to enrich life for all by delivering optimal memory and storage systems for a wide range of applications, from AI and the cloud to the intelligent edge.

old_description: Mid-South Medical Imaging, LLC is the oldest and largest independent medical imaging company in our area.
about:
Mid-South Medical Imaging, LLC, originally founded as Mid-South X-Ray in 1968, is headquartered in Flowood, Mississippi. The company operates additional branches in Birmingham, Alabama, and Memphis, Tennessee, serving healthcare providers across Mississippi, Alabama, Arkansas, Louisiana, western Tennessee, and the Florida panhandle.

The company distributes a broad range of medical imaging equipment, including digital radiography rooms and portables, R/F systems, radiology and point-of-care ultrasound, CT, MRI, mammography, and C-arm systems. It carries thousands of healthcare products from manufacturers such as Adaptix and Samsung, and employs registered x-ray technologists who provide applications training for the equipment it sells. Service capabilities include phone and email support as well as remote support technology for rapid troubleshooting.

Mid-South Medical Imaging primarily serves hospitals, orthopedic practices, and women's health facilities. Its product lineup features the Adaptix Ortho350 portable 3D orthopedic imaging system, the Samsung R20 AI-powered general imaging ultrasound, and the Samsung GM85 Fit mobile X-ray unit. The company also supplies 3D mammography, upright stereotactic biopsy, and breast ultrasound workstations for women's health programs.

The company emphasizes "Southern service, digital-age support," highlighting its focus on quality customer relations and post-sale service.

name: Midwest Precision Molding
old_description: Proud to Be Wisconsin's Leading Provider of Plastic Injection Molding
about:
The company has provided plastic injection molding services for over 40 years, with CEO Larry Austin the business since at least 2016 when he acquired Tri-Tec Corp. in nearby Darien and expanded the Plasti-Coil building. The firm began as a specialist in coil winding bobbins and grew into a full-service custom molder.

The shop runs more than 40 injection molding presses, including 11 Sodick machines and new automation cells, supported by an on-site tool room. Core capabilities include tight-tolerance molding of gears, bobbins, and insert-overmolded parts, plus a recently added Bausano extrusion line for tubing. Secondary operations such as terminal and pin insertion are performed on specialized equipment, and the company reports producing millions of bobbins annually across high- and low-volume projects.

The company emphasizes collaboration from product design and material selection through post-production, serving any project size without minimum order constraints mentioned.

MPM positions itself as Wisconsin's only true custom molder focused on tight-tolerance precision parts, a distinction reinforced by its ISO 9001:2015 certified quality system and UL Assurance Seal. The business was built to keep injection molding and moldmaking in the Midwest, offering in-house tooling and rapid response from concept to delivery.

name: Mississippi Silicon
old_description: Mississippi Silicon is the first domestic manufacturer of raw silicon metal built in the past 40 years and produces approximately 10% of all silicon metal used in the United States.
about:
Mississippi Silicon operates a silicon metal production facility in Burnsville, Mississippi. The plant launched in late 2015, becoming the first new domestic silicon metal smelter built in the United States in four decades. The company is structured as a partnership between Rima Holding USA, Inc. (the majority owner, linked to Brazilian ferroalloy producer Rima Industrial S/A) and Clean Tech I LLC, a group of strategic investors and financial advisers.

The facility produces raw silicon metal using submerged electric arc furnaces that reduce quartz or gravel (SiO₂) with a carbon source to yield 99% pure molten silicon, which is tapped in batches. Mississippi Silicon invested over $200 million in the Burnsville site and now supplies roughly 10% of the silicon metal consumed in the U.S. The operation emphasizes modern furnace controls, proprietary process techniques, and automated off-gas containment to achieve low-cost, high-quality output.

The company sells silicon metal to customers that serve automotive, electronics, steel, and a broad range of consumer, industrial, and commercial markets across North America and globally. Automotive manufacturing is cited as a key end-use sector, alongside electronics and steel production.

Mississippi Silicon was established to restore domestic silicon metal supply, leveraging low-cost Tennessee Valley Authority electricity, proximity to raw-material sources in Mississippi, Alabama, and Kentucky, and advanced automation to become one of the world’s lowest-cost and highest-quality producers. The venture also aims to create jobs in northeast Mississippi.

Mississippi Solar, LLC is based in Eupora, Mississippi. The company was founded in 2008 by Will and Carolyn Hegman and officially registered with the Mississippi Secretary of State in 2009. It was the first commercial electrical contractor in the state to receive a Specialty Wind & Solar classification. Today the business is owned and operated by John and Virginia Wilbanks, both Mississippi natives, and remains family-owned.

The firm designs and installs turn-key solar photovoltaic and battery-backup systems for residential and commercial customers across Mississippi. It also sells, installs, and services Generac home and business standby generators in more than 20 counties, and fits Level 2 and 3 EV charging stations, energy-management thermostats, and LP-tank monitoring. The company acts as a commercial electrical contractor and residential builder, handling permitting, project management, and ongoing system monitoring.

Mississippi Solar serves homeowners, businesses, farms, and institutional clients. Early projects included a poultry farm, a sports arena, and the state's first commercial utility-scale solar PV system as well as the first grid-tie and grid-tie-with-battery installations under the TVA Generation Partners program. The company also supports generator customers in counties such as Lafayette, Pontotoc, Lee, and Lowndes.

The company emphasizes its local roots and code expertise, NABCEP-certified installers, and status as a Generac Power Pro Elite Plus dealer. It backs installations with a 25-year module warranty through REC Solar, lifetime system monitoring, and a five-year workmanship warranty. Its stated mission is to empower customers with reliable, worry-free energy independence, sustainability, and backup power.

Mobius serves electronics manufacturers, including IoT module makers and hardware manufacturers. The company differentiates itself by vetting suppliers and comprehensively testing part authenticity, offering 10–70% off common parts at market rates, and providing access to rare stock from other manufacturers' excess. about:
Modern Edge Metal Fabrication operates from a 6,000-square-foot shop in West Bath, Maine. The company traces its roots to 2015 when Luke Winne, a Georgetown native who grew up around his father’s machine shop, launched a one-man operation out of his dad’s 16-by-24-foot building after a decade honing his craft in Montana. Winne incorporated the business in 2020, and his wife Mandy joined the family-owned venture in 2021.

The shop provides full-service metal fabrication — architectural, structural, marine, and production work — using MIG, TIG, and stick welding (including portable units), a manual lathe, knee mill, 48-inch sheet metal brake (11-gauge mild steel capacity), 80-ton ironworker, 13-by-21-inch band saw, plasma cutting, and 3D modeling. A small team of craftsmen handles design, engineering, fabrication, finishing, and installation in-house.

Customers include general contractors, architects, marine contractors, shipyards, furniture designers, and agricultural operators such as wild blueberry and vegetable farms. The company has fabricated and installed over 8,000 lineal feet of cable railing in midcoast Maine and built the 18-foot Cape Elizabeth Lighthouse replica for the Maine Maritime Museum’s permanent exhibit.

Winne founded Modern Edge to turn a childhood passion for metalworking into a business built on long-term relationships and word-of-mouth referrals. The firm emphasizes a design-through-install workflow, mirror-finish stainless capabilities with in-house passivation, and a proprietary cable rail system priced competitively with national brands.

about:
Mom's Meals, operating as PurFoods LLC, is headquartered in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma. The company has spent over 25 years developing food-as-medicine solutions aimed at reducing nutrition insecurity and improving health outcomes at home. While its exact founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed, the organization describes its origin as a mission to help people live healthier lives through delicious, nutritious food, education, and caring support.

The company produces medically tailored meals, shelf-stable meals, produce and pantry boxes, oral nutrition supplements, and halal and kosher meal options. Its nine menus offer more than 60 meal choices designed by registered dietitians and professional chefs. Production takes place in USDA- and FDA-inspected facilities across a network of locations strategically placed to enable nationwide delivery. In 2025, the company donated 59,863 medically tailored meals to individuals experiencing nutrition insecurity and provided 5,415 shelf-stable meals for Hurricane Helene relief in Georgia.

Mom's Meals serves health plans, Area Agencies on Aging (AAAs), state governments, case managers, health care professionals, and individuals with caregivers. Concrete partnerships include AmeriHealth Caritas District of Columbia, where medically tailored meals reduced health care costs and readmissions, and the Maui County Office on Aging, recognized through a USAging Community Champion Award. The company also collaborates with Blue Shield of California Promise Health Plan to deliver shelf-stable meals in wildfire aftermath.

The company emphasizes evidence-based solutions that meet specific dietary needs, taste great, and reliably reach homes others cannot. Its differentiation rests on comprehensive food-as-medicine offerings that combine meals, nutrition counseling, and education to improve health outcomes, lower total cost of care, and bring comfort and dignity to those served.

about:
Montana Gluten Free operates from Belgrade, Montana, where it runs a dedicated gluten-free milling and packaging facility. The company was built around a "farm to fork" purity protocol that controls the supply chain from field practices through finished goods, though a founding year and founder names are not disclosed in public materials.

The company produces gluten-free oat ingredients and baking mixes, including an All Purpose Baking Mix and Gluten Free Cream of Oats. Oats are grown on contract farms that have not planted gluten-containing grains for four years; fields are hand-rogued twice and harvested with dedicated or thoroughly cleaned equipment. Every load is tested at harvest, in transit, and on arrival using 500-gram visual inspections and in-house assays, with third-party confirmation from labs such as Romer, FARRP, and AGQ Labs. The facility itself is certified by the Gluten-Free Certification Organization (GFCO) and handles none of the top nine allergens or corn.

Montana Gluten Free sells wholesale to grocery stores, retailers, bakeries, granola bar manufacturers, and other food producers seeking certified gluten-free, high-protein ingredients. The company emphasizes its purity protocol and glyphosate-free sourcing as the basis for its appeal to brands that require stringent allergen and contaminant controls.

The business states its purpose is to provide high-quality, safe food through a transparent, controlled supply chain — from field rotation and clean-out tickets at harvest to duplicate testing before milling and final third-party verification.

Its portfolio spans all forms of actuation technology—electric, hydraulic, and electro-hydrostatic—along with sophisticated control electronics and system software. The company operates as a integrator of precision motion control systems across four business segments: Military Aircraft, Commercial Aircraft, Space and Defense, and Industrial.

Moog serves customers in military and commercial aviation, space and defense programs, and industrial machinery markets. Concrete examples include flight control systems for military aircraft and rotorcraft, critical control products for commercial jets and business jets, motion and flow control solutions for space and defense platforms, and high-performance motion control products for next-generation industrial machines.

The company traces its differentiation to a founding culture of persistence and creativity, where the word "can't" was not accepted. Moog emphasizes a collaborative approach to solving difficult motion control problems, seeks long-term partnerships, and maintains a global footprint with local customer support. Its stated values—trust, communication, and shared success—underpin its engineering and business practices.

about:
North Dakota Telephone Company (NDTC) began operation in 1993 as a multi-faceted telecommunications provider headquartered in Devils Lake, North Dakota. The company is owned by a consortium of three area telephone cooperatives—United Telephone Mutual Aid Cooperative of Langdon, Dakota Central Rural Telephone Cooperative of Carrington, and Polar Communications of Park River—giving it a locally rooted ownership structure.

NDTC delivers a suite of communications services including unlimited local and long-distance telephone, high-speed internet access, digital television, computer networking and wiring, website hosting, surveillance equipment, and dedicated data circuits. The company serves more than 11,000 customers across northeastern North Dakota with a staff of over 60 local employees who live and work in the communities they serve.

Its customer base spans residential subscribers, businesses, and community institutions throughout the region, including towns such as Cando, Fessenden, Harvey, Leeds, McVille, New Rockford, and Tolna. NDTC is also a member-owner of North Dakota Long Distance (NDLD) and Dakota Carrier Network (DCN), which provide statewide long-distance and carrier-grade Ethernet, wavelength, and Wi-Fi services. In 2003, NDTC helped establish North Plains Utility Contracting to handle underground construction for its network and other utilities.

The company emphasizes community reinvestment as a differentiator. Since 1995, its Dollars in Motion program has granted over $1 million to local schools, non-profits, and community projects, and it awards ten $1,000 scholarships annually to graduating seniors. Employees volunteer regularly, sponsor local events, and partner with food banks and sports leagues. NDTC’s stated mission is to provide a quality communication network that strengthens communities, guided by core values of reliability, service, accountability, integrity, growth, and communication.

about:
NPI Solutions was founded in May 2000 by Kevin Andersen in Morgan Hill, California, in the heart of Silicon Valley. Andersen, who had spent years in the personal computer and cable assembly boom, started the company to fill a niche for a reliable, high-throughput American manufacturer of custom electronic assemblies. The business began in a 4,000-square-foot facility and expanded globally, opening locations in Suzhou, China (2008), Singapore (2013), and Nogales, Mexico (2024). In 2022, NPI became part of the Amphenol family of companies, a global provider of interconnect, sensor, and antenna solutions.

The company specializes in complex cable assemblies, discrete wire harnesses, and full electro-mechanical box builds. Its capabilities span design engineering (mechanical, electrical, and process), prototyping, quick-turn assembly, and low-volume, high-mix production. NPI operates a Class 10,000 clean room at its Morgan Hill headquarters, supporting contamination-sensitive work for semiconductor and medical device customers. The firm also provides on-site engineering and technician services throughout Silicon Valley, with 24/7 emergency support for established clients.

NPI serves industries including semiconductor, medical device, robotics, power delivery, automotive, aerospace, IT, data communications, and military. Its customer base ranges from startups to Fortune 500 companies, with a strong concentration among Silicon Valley technology firms that require custom electro-mechanical components and secure, on-site collaboration.

NPI’s stated mission is to provide alternative manufacturing solutions that improve supply-chain efficiency and cost through flexible real-time systems, concurrent engineering, and design-for-manufacturability practices. The company emphasizes quick response times, first-rate production, experienced engineering, and data privacy—particularly for semiconductor clients—as key differentiators.

National Power Equipment, Inc. (NPE) operates from Cleveland, Ohio, where it was founded in 1994. The company began with a simple realization: industrial customers do not merely need equipment, they need a reliable source for solutions to fix and maintain large switchgear and circuit breakers.

The company supplies used and remanufactured air and vacuum circuit breakers, substation switchgear, protective relays, and related parts. NPE specializes in low‑voltage (600 V AC or less) through medium‑voltage (15 kV) equipment, carrying product lines from every major U.S. manufacturer dating back to 1940. Beyond distribution, it manufactures a growing aftermarket parts list (AFT) that upgrades commonly failing components with modern materials, and it offers reconditioning services, rental and exchange programs, quick‑ship inventory, and technical manuals. The firm also provides 24/7 emergency support and assistance with both scheduled and unscheduled outages.

Customers span the full spectrum of the electrical industry, including industrial plants, utilities, and government agencies. NPE is an approved U.S. Government vendor (CAGE code 84AC4), indicating a track record with federal buyers.

The company differentiates itself by focusing on tailored, cost‑effective solutions rather than simple product sales. Its aftermarket parts are engineered to eliminate original design weaknesses, and real‑time inventory visibility lets buyers confirm availability instantly.

about:
Nebraska Public Power District (NPPD) is a publicly-owned utility headquartered in Columbus, Nebraska. It was formed on January 1, 1970, through the merger of Consumers Public Power District, Platte Valley Public Power and Irrigation District, and Nebraska Public Power System. As a political subdivision of the State of Nebraska, NPPD is governed by an 11-member Board of Directors elected from its chartered territory, which spans all or parts of 84 of the state's 93 counties.

NPPD generates, transmits, and distributes electric power across its service territory. Its generation portfolio includes wind, coal, hydroelectric, nuclear, and natural gas facilities, providing a diverse mix of baseload and renewable energy. The utility operates customer service centers throughout the state, offering call answering, dispatch, and start/stop services for both NPPD and partner utilities. It serves more than 95,000 retail customers directly and provides wholesale power to 35 municipalities and 23 public power districts or cooperatives.

NPPD also administers energy efficiency programs like EnergyWise, which offers incentives for smart thermostats and lawn equipment.

New England Table Company operates from a studio in Londonderry, New Hampshire. The business was founded by Ronald Lohse, a former software engineer who turned a woodworking hobby into a full-time practice after years of building digital systems. Lohse’s first shop stood on the shore of a small New Hampshire lake, where the rhythm of hand tools and the scent of walnut rekindled a childhood memory of watching his grandfather, watercolorist Henry Lohse, build paintings layer by layer.

The company produces custom hardwood tables — dining, coffee, console, desk, and conference pieces — along with matching chairs. Each piece is built by hand in the Londonderry studio using live-edge slabs, book-matched pairs, and river-table constructions. The workflow moves from an initial conversation and digital rendering through wood selection, joinery, and hand-applied finish, with clients receiving photographic updates via a private portal. To date, more than 150 tables have been delivered.

Clients include homeowners, interior designers, and trade professionals across New England. A dedicated trade program supports designers specifying pieces for residential and light commercial projects, while the Atelier Experience offers a higher-touch commission tier in which Lohse personally sources the slab and oversees every design decision.

Lohse started the company on the conviction that furniture should be kept for generations, not replaced. That philosophy drives the Zero Waste Collection, which repurposes offcuts into smaller objects, and the practice of personally delivering and installing each table throughout the region so the maker sees the piece settle into its home.

New Mexico Manufacturing Extension Partnership (New Mexico MEP) operates from Albuquerque, New Mexico. As the official representative of the MEP National Network in the state, it functions as a NIST MEP approved center. The organization is structured as a public-private partnership that brings together government, not-for-profit, and industry resources.

The center delivers advisory and technical services to small and mid-sized manufacturers. Its offerings include process optimization, product development, scale-up processes, lean methodologies, workforce development, growth services, efficiency improvements, quality management systems, manufacturing safety, supply chain assistance, and connection to resources. Services are provided at reduced cost through a network of resource partners.

Clients span various manufacturing sectors in New Mexico. Examples include Old Barrel Tea Company in Albuquerque, which reported a 30% increase in online sales; Los Poblanos in Los Ranchos, which saw improved output and cycle time; Wicked Edge, a precision knife-sharpening equipment maker serving law enforcement and outdoor markets; and Navajo Spirit in Gallup, producing traditional-inspired clothing. The center also collaborates with companies such as TEAM Technologies, Alaska Structures, Valencia Flour Mill, Insight Lighting, OBG Architectural Millwork, and Santa Fe Spirits.

New Mexico MEP distinguishes itself through its affiliation with the MEP National Network, which the W.E. Upjohn Institute found delivered a 13.6-to-1 return on investment in 2020. The center emphasizes hands-on assistance and technology-driven solutions to help manufacturers overcome growth barriers.

about:
New Tech Metals operates from New Franken, Wisconsin, where it was founded in 1982 as New Tech Metalworks. The company is a veteran-owned, family-owned small business. Ownership passed to the Blackman family in 2003 when brothers Jeff, Keith, and David Blackman acquired the shop. Today, the second generation — Adam and Andy Blackman, both U.S. Army veterans, and their cousin Derek Blackman — own and run the operation. Adam served as a 19D Cavalry Scout and Andy as a 19K M1 Armor Crewman, experience they say informs the discipline applied to every part.

The shop provides six in-house capabilities: design and development, cutting (laser, turret punch, plasma), forming (press brakes), welding (AWS-certified across nine codes), CNC machining (milling and turning), and assembly with finishing. Equipment includes a 5-ton overhead crane, Mitsubishi fiber lasers, Strippit turret, Safan Darley press brakes, Haas VMC and EC-500 machining centers, FANUC robotic welding cells, and Haeger/Timesavers finishing systems. The facility added a 7,000-square-foot office expansion in 2012 and maintains in-house material stock. Production focuses on low- to mid-volume, high-reliability components for defense and industrial OEMs.

New Tech Metals serves three core sectors. In defense, it supplies Tier-2 components to OEMs and prime contractors for over 20 vehicle platforms, shipboard infrastructure, weapons support equipment, communications enclosures, and structural assemblies. Transportation customers include fire apparatus, refuse vehicles, concrete mixers, cargo trailers, airport ground-support equipment, and automotive programs. For machine and equipment builders, the shop produces parts for packaging equipment, paper converting, drying and curing systems, commercial appliances, power equipment, and material handling systems.

The company emphasizes that its veteran ownership brings a culture of accountability and precision that goes beyond standard quality certifications. It operates under a single ITAR-registered roof with DFARS material compliance, NIST/CMMC cybersecurity controls, and ISO 9001:2015 quality management. The owners quote jobs directly and remain accountable through delivery, offering one quote, one schedule, and one team from print to packout.

Newport Industries, LLC operates from West Branch, Iowa, as a family‑owned small business. The company does not publish a founding date, but notes that its team brings 100 years of combined experience in metal design, fabrication, and machining.

The shop provides design, engineering, fabrication, machining, and artistic metalwork capabilities under one roof. It functions as an original equipment manufacturer, producing three proprietary lines: Industrial Pulley Puller hydraulic gear pullers for maintenance departments, Newport Car Wash stainless‑steel parts and accessories for self‑service car washes, and Newport Living architectural metal products such as TV mounts. Contract manufacturing services are also offered for outside clients.

Primary markets include the self‑service car wash industry, which receives rugged, all‑weather stainless components, and industrial maintenance teams that use the hydraulic pullers to remove frozen gears, bearings, and couplings.

Newtown Apparel emphasizes a "no-hassle" model that combines a dedicated account contact, free artwork assistance, and free online-store setup so clients can move from idea to finished goods without managing multiple vendors.

name: Niagara Power Transformer Corp.
old_description: Liquid-filled power, distribution, auto-, instrument, and specialty transformers up to 500 MVA
about:
Niagara Power Transformer Corp. traces its roots to 1924, when John H. Darby founded Erie Electric Corp. in Buffalo, New York, with $300 in borrowed capital. The company designed its first Niagara industrial transformer in 1933 and its first utility-grade transformer in 1943. Leadership passed to Fred W. Darby in 1979 and then to John F. Darby in 2000, marking three generations of family ownership. In 2024 the firm celebrated its 100-year anniversary and joined the Quanta Services family; Chris Kraft assumed the presidency in 2025.

The company manufactures liquid-filled power, distribution, auto-, instrument, and specialty transformers with ratings up to 500 MVA and voltages up to 138 kV. Its product range includes rectifier duty, grounding, voltage regulator, and special-application transformers such as mobile substation, hazardous-location, and furnace-duty units. A $45 million production campus opened in Buffalo between 2013 and 2018, followed by a $4 million advanced engineering center in 2019 and a further $50 million in recent facility upgrades. The site features a multiple-bay test facility with an RF room, a positive-pressure winding shop with humidity and particulate control, and a paint booth meeting IEEE and UL standards. The company reports completing its 75,000th transformer in 2000 and serves more than 80 countries.

Niagara Power Transformer serves a broad set of industries, including electric utilities, renewables (wind, solar, geothermal), oil and gas, petrochemical, mining, nuclear, marine offshore, mass transit, military, aerospace, automotive, and heavy industrial sectors such as steel, cement, and pulp and paper.

The firm emphasizes engineering depth — citing over 400 years of combined design experience and 700 years of manufacturing experience among its staff — and notes that its technical consultant is an IEEE Fellow active in standards committees. It highlights a test-floor failure rate of 3.25% and a field failure rate of 0.15% over the past decade, along with ISO 9001:2015 certification and numerous third-party approvals (UL, CSA, DNV, ABS, Lloyd’s Register, etc.). Differentiators include quick proposal turnaround, engineered-to-order flexibility, full bonding capability, in-house PE certification, and physical segregation of clean and dirty production areas.

name: Niltronix Circuits
old_description: Niltronix Circuits is committed to pioneering total turnkey solutions and fostering collaborative partnerships with each of our customers to ensure the timely delivery of top-tier quality products.
about:
Niltronix Circuits, based in Sugar Land, Texas, was founded in 1982 as a woman-owned small business. The company began with a focus on delivering quality printed circuit solutions with rapid turnarounds for the oil and gas and industrial sectors.

Today, Niltronix operates a 24,000-square-foot facility in West Houston where it fabricates rigid, flex, and rigid-flex printed circuit boards and provides full turnkey assembly services. Its capabilities span PCB fabrication, surface-mount and through-hole assembly, box-build and cable-harness integration, and a suite of in-house testing including burn-in, functional, temperature-cycling, shock, vibration, and environmental screening. Additional value-added services include conformal coating, potting, programming, and staking, with a specialization in high-temperature, high-reliability assemblies. The shop handles everything from quick-turn prototypes to full production runs.

The company serves aerospace, medical, oil and gas, renewable energy, and industrial customers.

Niltronix differentiates itself by acting as an extension of its customers' operations, emphasizing collaborative partnerships, on-time delivery, and a quality system certified to AS9100 Rev D and ISO 9001:2015.

old_description: Solar, battery backup, EV charging, and service for Louisiana homes and businesses.
about:
Nola Solar Energy is a New Orleans, Louisiana-based solar installation and service company founded by a team with over seven years of hands-on industry experience. The locally owned and operated business was built around a practical approach to solar, battery backup, EV charging, and long-term system support.

The company provides turnkey solar systems for homes and small businesses, including design, permitting, and code-compliant installation. It also installs battery backup systems tailored to essential loads, Level 2 EV chargers with panel assessment and wiring, and offers a full suite of service work: inspection, troubleshooting, repair, cleaning, panel removal and reinstall, inverter and monitoring support, and system upgrades.

Nola Solar Energy serves residential homeowners and small commercial customers across Louisiana and the Gulf South. Its projects range from new rooftop solar arrays and battery storage for outage protection to EV charger installations and service calls for existing systems originally installed by other providers. The company also supports off-grid power projects and commercial parking-lot solar structures.

The firm emphasizes its licensed and insured electrical team, brand-certified installer status for major solar, battery, and inverter equipment, and a sales-plus-service model that handles both new installations and ongoing maintenance. Customers frequently cite quick response times, clear communication, and a structured service process as key differentiators.

name: Nomad Furniture
old_description: Handcrafted from solid hardwoods, finished with zero-VOC materials, and engineered for a lifetime.
about:
Nomad Furniture operates from Farr West, Utah, where the Mitchell family relocated the business in 2019 after purchasing it from Albuquerque bed maker Dave Cady. Cady had built the brand over more than 30 years in New Mexico before retiring. Connor Mitchell, joined by his parents Ken and Ana, trained with Cady and moved the operation to northern Utah, establishing a family-owned shop where every member contributes.

The company handcrafts platform beds and nightstands from solid North American hardwoods — oak, maple, and other species — using zero-VOC finishes such as Daddy Van’s all-natural hemp oil and Rubio products. Each piece is designed and built in their Utah workshop, featuring upgraded premium rails, slats, and a center leg for added strength. No veneers, particleboard, or upcycled woods are used.

Nomad Furniture sells directly to residential customers seeking durable, non-toxic bedroom furniture. Reviews highlight buyers who appreciate the solid construction, easy assembly, and healthy finishes, with one customer noting the bed handled a heavy latex mattress without issue. The company ships free anywhere in the continental United States.

After a devastating shop fire in June 2024 destroyed all equipment and materials, the Mitchells rebuilt with the help of son-in-law Jake, an engineer. The recovery led to refined designs and a renewed commitment to zero-VOC materials, positioning the company around resilience, American craftsmanship, and a healthier home environment.

name: Nordic Semiconductor, Inc
old_description: Advanced State-of-Health battery monitoring and fleet-wide observability
about:
Nordic Semiconductor, Inc. operates from Portland, Oregon, where it develops ultra-low-power wireless semiconductors and cloud services for the Internet of Things. The company does not disclose its founding year or ownership structure in public materials.

The firm designs and supplies system-on-chips (SoCs), system-in-packages (SiPs), and pre-certified modules — including the nRF54L series, the dual-core nRF5340, and the nRF93M1 Cat 1 bis cellular modem — alongside the nPM1300 power management IC. Its nRF Cloud platform, built on Memfault technology, provides chip-to-cloud device management, embedded observability, location services, and lifetime flat-rate FOTA updates. The latest nRF54LM20B integrates an Axon neural processing unit for on-device machine learning.

Nordic’s components appear in consumer, healthcare, industrial, and educational devices. The BBC micro:bit, now in its tenth year with Nordic silicon, has reached 73 million students worldwide. Other deployments include See.Sense’s NB-IoT cycle tracker, MEZOO’s remote cardiac monitoring system, Polar’s multisport watches, Lynxemi’s industrial asset-health sensors, Bettear’s Auracast audio streamers, eCozy’s Matter-enabled smart thermostats, and the IDR01 smart ring.

The company emphasizes ultra-low power consumption, integrated cloud connectivity, and a unified software ecosystem as its core differentiators, aiming to shorten time-to-market for IoT developers through pre-certified hardware and a single SDK across multiple wireless protocols.

Based in Rockford, Iowa, North Iowa Fabrication operates as a laser-based fabrication shop.

The shop provides in-house laser cutting, CNC machining (milling, drilling, tapping, boring, turning), CNC brake press forming, welding (MIG, TIG, spot), powder coating, painting, and assembly. Automated "lights-out" laser cutting and nitrogen-assisted cutting for scale-free edges are cited as cost and time advantages.

name: North Star Systems, Inc.
about:
North Star Systems, Inc. was founded in 1997 in Pelham, Alabama, by the former management team of SRT Electro-Optics, Inc., a subsidiary of Southern Research. The small business operates from the Birmingham area and was established to serve commercial, industrial, and defense clients with engineering and production services.

The company provides electronic circuit design, embedded software development, electro-optics, servo controls, and video signal processing. Its capabilities span prototype hardware development, transition-to-production, production test equipment design, quality assurance documentation, and configuration management. North Star has delivered projects ranging from video recording equipment controllers and infrared target collection systems to remote weapon stations, gun control units, and airborne fire-retardant dispensing controls.

Customers include U.S. Army programs such as the Integrated Sensor Architecture, missile and ground vehicle platforms, naval vessels, and aircraft systems. The firm also serves the nuclear power sector (independent verification and validation), commercial video recording and editing equipment manufacturers, welding machine tool builders, and firefighting air-tanker operators. Work has covered DISA STIG compliance, MISB metadata standards, and electromagnetic compatibility testing.

North Star emphasizes its 30-plus years of aerospace and defense experience and its ability to redesign products for parts obsolescence while adding new features. The team focuses on solving challenging problems to make customers successful, offering a responsive, experienced crew that can take a concept through live-fire testing and full-rate production.

name: Northe Woodworking
old_description: We partner with architects, interior designers, and homeowners to bring custom cabinetry and millwork to life across New England and beyond.
about:
Northe Woodworking operates from an 8,500-square-foot workshop in Lewiston, Maine. The company began with a handful of tools and a commitment to traditional craftsmanship, but a fire at its original Mechanic Falls shop forced a restart after one year. That setback sharpened the team’s focus and deepened their dedication to building cabinetry that feels as though it has always belonged in a space.

The studio produces custom cabinetry, architectural millwork, built-in furniture, kitchens, and vanities, scaling from single pieces to full-home millwork packages. A full team of craftspeople works in the Lewiston facility, handling design, fabrication, and finishing for projects that range from traditional to contemporary styles.

Northe serves architects, interior designers, and homeowners throughout New England and the broader Northeast, including Maine, Massachusetts, New York, and Connecticut. Recent collaborations have included a Brooklyn brownstone renovation and a new coastal Maine build, illustrating the geographic reach of their client base.

The founders started the business on the idea that great cabinetry should quietly elevate a room and last for decades, reflecting the same care as the rest of the home. That philosophy, combined with a collaborative process that involves clients at every stage, is what the company says distinguishes its work.

about:
Northwest Lumber Company has operated from the same Indianapolis, Indiana location since Harry Greeley and his wife Eva founded the business in 1956. What began as a mom-and-pop hardware store selling construction-grade plywood and lumber transitioned over the decades into a specialty supplier of furniture-grade hardwoods, cabinet-grade plywood, exotic tone-woods for instrument building, and fine woodworking hand tools. The company remains family-owned, now managed by the third generation of Greeleys.

The company stocks hardwood lumber graded Selects & Better, along with cabinet-grade plywood and a selection of exotic tone-woods suited for musical instruments, fine cabinetry, furniture, and boat building. It also carries a curated line of fine woodworking hand tools. No facility size, headcount, or annual volume figures are published.

Customers include furniture makers, luthiers, cabinet shops, and boat builders seeking high-grade hardwoods and specialty tone-woods. The firm serves both professional woodworkers and hobbyists through its retail showroom, which is open Monday through Friday 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. and Saturday mornings.

The shift from construction materials to fine woodworking supplies was driven by the arrival of big-box retailers in the market. Northwest Lumber Company is a member of the Indiana Hardwood Lumbermen's Association, reflecting a stated commitment to sustainable forest productivity and the production of high-quality hardwood products.

about:
O&G Studio operates from a factory in Warren, Rhode Island. The company was founded in 2009 by Jonathan Glatt and Sara Ossana. The studio produces a full range of seating, tables, lighting, decorative accents, and cabinet hardware. Its hardware collections — including Cygnet, Atlantic, and Cleat — are crafted in solid brass with a variety of finishes.

O&G serves interior designers, architects, and collectors worldwide through trade accounts and direct specification. The firm's work has been specified in projects featured by The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, Architectural Digest, Elle Decor, Wallpaper, Dwell, and other design publications. Vogue named Glatt one of ten contemporary designers to collect today.

The company positions its output as modern heirlooms rooted in authenticity, place, and the wisdom of history as a foundation for invention. Glatt's singular vision combines memory and invention, celebrating New England's design legacy while creating work that is new, surprising, and uniquely its own.

ORACLE Lighting operates from Metairie, Louisiana, where it designs, engineers, manufactures primary housing components, and assembles complete automotive lighting products. The company does not disclose its founding year or ownership structure in the provided materials.

OrthoTek Inc. was founded in 2001 in Des Moines, Iowa. The company began as a supplier of durable home medical equipment, aiming to connect independent contractors with the products their patients need.

OrthoTek distributes a range of durable medical equipment including off-the-shelf bracing, continuous passive motion devices, bone growth stimulation systems, compression therapy units, and negative pressure wound therapy devices. All products are sourced from manufacturers and carry original warranties. The company offers both purchase and rental options, and assists customers with insurance paperwork to secure reimbursement.

The primary customers are independent contractors, hospitals, and physicians’ offices that serve patients requiring home medical equipment. OrthoTek’s focus is on the home healthcare and durable medical equipment sectors, providing equipment that helps patients recover from acute injuries or manage chronic conditions.

The company’s stated mission emphasizes affordability and accessibility, ensuring equipment can be obtained whether the patient rents or buys. OrthoTek is a recognized partner of the Community Health Accreditation Program, which accredits community-based healthcare businesses. With over two decades of experience, the firm positions itself as a reliable link between manufacturers and end users.
